correctness.rationale: The standard integral blowup of P1 x P1 at (0,0),(1,1),(infinity,infinity) is the split M0,5 compactification. The marking transposition exchanges factors. Away from the three exceptional curves, its fixed ideal is the diagonal. On every exceptional chart the complete equalizer ideal is (x(r-1),(r-1)(r+1)); it becomes (xt,t(t+2)), the intersection of the horizontal divisor ideal (t) and the horizontal section ideal (x,t+2) over Z. Fixed directions r=+/-1 exhaust every exceptional point; all lie in this chart. The local algebra has Z-module form Z[x] plus Z*t and hence is flat. Modulo 2 it is k[x,t]/(xt,t^2), giving precisely one embedded length-one nilradical at each of three disjoint points. The derivative is the identity modulo 2 yet the formal action contains the nonzero xt term, proving non-linearizability. Direct executable symbolic checks and complete prime-field blowup enumeration independently support the proof.

value.rationale: The whole fixed scheme of the canonical marking transposition is a natural invariant of the quintessential degree-five del Pezzo/moduli surface. The collision of three tame isolated fixed points with a positive-dimensional fixed divisor in characteristic two produces three embedded length-one associated points despite integral flatness. This exact phenomenon is invisible to reduced fixed loci and to the derivative, yielding a motivated wild local-boundary obstruction to formal linearization. It informs possible wild quotient and moduli degeneration analyses without claiming those results.
